units.function: Unit tests for normalizing and delegating sandbox-provider plugin configuration validation when a schema field uses the secret-ref format.
units.dependencyDirection: Stored/user provider config enters plugin-environment-driver; the host locates a ready driver manifest, rewrites structured secret bindings, then calls the plugin worker's environmentValidateConfig and trusts its normalized configuration response.
units.keyDataModels: Sandbox environment driver manifest/configSchema; apiKey string with secret-ref format; structured secret_ref secretId/version; bare UUID or raw provider-key string; plugin normalizedConfig.
units.lifecycle: Find a ready provider; convert latest reference object to a bare ID; reject pinned numeric version; pass config to a running plugin for validation/normalization; return normalized output.
units.testAssessment: All three tests pass and document current compatibility behavior, but that behavior collapses two security types: a secret reference becomes a bare string while raw secret strings are also accepted and forwarded unchanged. The plugin cannot distinguish intent by type, and the schema's secret-ref format is not an enforcement boundary. Missing are secret ownership/tenant/target checks, prohibited plaintext, schema strictness, malicious normalized output, version/rotation semantics, side-effect-free validation, timeout and log/error redaction.
units.designRationale: Maintain compatibility with plugin validators expecting a string identifier while accepting newer structured secret binding objects and disallowing unsupported pinned versions.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS local execution must keep credentials out of control-plane/plugin configuration and preserve typed secret-reference semantics until an authorized execution node resolves the exact secret for a specific run.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT lossy conversion to bare strings and plaintext acceptance. Define an opaque SecretHandle schema containing provider-neutral reference ID, tenant, audience, purpose, selector and policy version, signed or issued by SecretPort. Plugin config validation receives only metadata such as presence/capability, never raw value or globally meaningful secret ID. Runtime resolution occurs just-in-time on the bound local node after Work/Contract/permission/data checks, yields short-lived material, and never round-trips through normalized config. Reject plaintext for secret fields; validate strict schemas and plugin-normalized output; audit access and rotation/revocation.
units.responsibilityConflict: A plugin may receive either an actual credential or a reusable secret identifier with no work, human, permission, purpose or action binding. This makes it impossible to prove which authorized secret was used for which responsible execution.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL type-confusion: structured secret_ref is downgraded to a bare string indistinguishable from a raw secret. CRITICAL plaintext path: a raw provider key is explicitly accepted and sent to plugin validation despite secret-ref schema format. HIGH tenant/auth gap: secret existence, Company ownership, target audience and capability are not checked in this unit. HIGH plugin-trust gap: plugin-normalized config is accepted without proving secret types remain safe. HIGH lifecycle gap: only latest is supported and rotation/revocation race semantics are absent. MEDIUM validation gap: strict JSON schema/additional fields and malicious plugin errors/timeouts are untested.
